core: The greenhouse effect: how it works, that it is natural and life-sustaining but being intensified by human emissions
The evidence for warming: instrumental temperature record, rising atmospheric CO2 (Keeling curve), ice loss, sea-level rise
The human cause: IPCC AR6 finding that human influence is unequivocally the dominant cause of observed warming (established consensus)
The distinction between mitigation and adaptation
The distinction between weather and climate
supporting: The difference between a baseline period and the pre-industrial reference (1850-1900)
Why single events are not the same as trends
That policy responses are contested and are attributed, not adjudicated
outOfScope: Individual greenhouse gases and global warming potential (owned by Greenhouse Gases topic)
Personal or organizational carbon footprint accounting (owned by Carbon Footprints topic)
Energy systems and renewable technology detail (owned by Energy Use and Renewable Energy topics)

claims.claim: The greenhouse effect is a natural process in which gases such as water vapor, carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, keeping Earth's surface roughly 33 C warmer than it would be otherwise; without it Earth would be frozen.

Human activities, principally emissions of greenhouse gases, have unequivocally caused global warming, with global surface temperature reaching about 1.1 C above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline in 2011-2020.
It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean, and land; the IPCC AR6 states human influence is the dominant cause of observed warming since the mid-20th century.

Continuous atmospheric CO2 measurements began at Mauna Loa in 1958 (the Keeling curve); the global annual mean atmospheric CO2 reached a record 422.8 ppm in 2024, up 3.75 ppm over 2023 (the largest annual increase in the record), versus a pre-industrial level near 280 ppm.

2024 was the warmest year in the instrumental record (since 1880); NASA/GISS estimated 2024 was about 1.47 C warmer than the mid-19th-century (1850-1900) average and about 1.28 C above its 1951-1980 baseline.

Global mean sea level has risen about 9.1 cm since satellite records began in 1993, and the rate of rise increased from about 2.1 mm/year in 1993 to about 4.5 mm/year in 2024, driven by thermal expansion of warming ocean water and melting land ice.

Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere at a place; climate is the long-term statistical pattern (typically 30 years or more) of weather. A single cold day does not refute a warming climate trend, and a single event cannot by itself be equated with climate change.

Responses to climate change fall into two complementary categories: mitigation (reducing or removing greenhouse-gas emissions to limit future warming) and adaptation (adjusting systems and behavior to reduce harm from changes already underway or unavoidable).

conflictingEvidence.issue: How best to respond to climate change (carbon pricing, subsidies, nuclear, regulation vs markets, degrowth) is politically contested.
positions: The lesson treats the core science (warming is happening and is human-caused) as established per IPCC and the science agencies.
Specific policy instruments are presented as attributed, contested options, not endorsed or ranked.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: State the settled science plainly; describe the mitigation/adaptation distinction neutrally and adjudicate no policy instrument.

rightsIssues: All sources are U.S. government agencies or the IPCC and are used as REFERENCE_ONLY: facts synthesized, prose written original. No source wording reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report (AR6), Summary for Policymakers
sourceRecords.notes: IPCC synthesis of AR6. Supports: human activities unequivocally caused ~1.1 C warming (2011-2020 vs 1850-1900); human influence dominant cause; mitigation vs adaptation framing. Read via ipcc.ch full-volume PDF and NASA-hosted accepted SYR copy (ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20230009525).

sourceRecords.title: Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis (AR6 WG1), Summary for Policymakers
sourceRecords.notes: AR6 Working Group 1 physical science basis. Supports the headline statement 'It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land' and the attribution of observed warming to human influence.

sourceRecords.title: Trends in Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide (Mauna Loa and global)
sourceRecords.notes: Primary CO2 record. Confirms continuous Mauna Loa measurements began March 1958 (Keeling). Global and Mauna Loa monthly/annual series. Used for the Keeling-curve narrative and dating of CO2 figures.

sourceRecords.title: During a Year of Extremes, Carbon Dioxide Levels Surge Faster than Ever
sourceRecords.notes: Supports: 2024 global annual mean CO2 = 422.8 ppm (record); +3.75 ppm over 2023, the largest one-year increase on record; Mauna Loa May 2024 seasonal peak 426.9 ppm.

sourceRecords.title: Temperatures Rising: NASA Confirms 2024 Warmest Year on Record
sourceRecords.provider: NASA / Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS)
sourceRecords.notes: Supports: 2024 warmest year since records began in 1880; ~1.28 C above 1951-1980 baseline; ~1.47 C above 1850-1900 mid-19th-century average. GISS maintains NASA's surface temperature record.

sourceRecords.title: NASA Uses 30-Year Satellite Record to Track and Project Rising Seas
sourceRecords.notes: Supports: global mean sea level up ~9.1 cm (3.6 in) since satellite altimetry began in 1993; rate rose from ~2.1 mm/yr (1993) to ~4.5 mm/yr (2024); driven by thermal expansion and land-ice melt.

sourceRecords.title: Climate Change: Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide
sourceRecords.notes: Explanatory source for how CO2 traps heat (greenhouse effect) and for the weather-vs-climate framing and the role of CO2 as the dominant long-lived warming agent.

sourceRecords.title: Carbon Dioxide (Earth Indicators)
sourceRecords.notes: Supports the greenhouse-effect explanation and the more-than-50% rise in CO2 since the 18th century (pre-industrial ~280 ppm to current ~420s ppm).
